title: Grizzly Hills
body: The Grizzly Hills roll north of the Howling Fjord, a land of towering pine forest, clear rivers and snowy heights, rich in lumber, ore and game, and both the Alliance and the Horde want all of it; they fight over the abandoned Venture Company logging sites and the port of Venture Bay while each looks for a road north. In the northwest the Drakkari trolls are dying to the Scourge, iron dwarves hold the east, and at the heart of the hills lie the remains of Vordrassil, a world tree the druids of old cut down.

title: Amberpine Lodge
body: Amberpine Lodge stands in the western hills, a remote lodge long used by hunters and woodsmen, now taken over by the Alliance military under a lieutenant who sees the war here as a deadlock. A Horde raid left its stores dangerously low. A druid of the lodge, whose ancestors, she says, planted the world tree Vordrassil, studies the taint its remains left in the earth.

parts.body: The Horde found the lodge's hidden stores through the eyes of the imperial eagles above the trees, and by the lieutenant's order the eagles were hunted down.

title: Conquest Hold
body: Conquest Hold is the stronghold of the Warsong Offensive in the western hills, raised to claim the region's lumber, ore and water for the Horde's war machine. Conqueror Krenna, aggressive even for an orc, commands with an iron hand: to her every soldier is a cog, and respect comes only from following orders without question. Her sister Gorgonna stands close by, and beside the hold the goblins stage pit fights.

parts.body: Krenna's rule ended in her own pit. She accused Gorgonna of neglecting her orders and turned on her before the crowd, and fell. Gorgonna said she had freed her people from a tyrant but lost a sister.

title: Silverbrook
body: Silverbrook is a village of trappers in the northwest of the hills, hardy folk who know the land better than any soldier, friendly to the Alliance and hostile to the Horde. An envoy has come from Amberpine Lodge to win them over. Not everyone from the village trusts it: a trapper's daughter, sent away by her father, hunts its people from a trading post to the east and says monsters killed him.

parts.body: Silverbrook's welcome was a mask. Its trappers are worgen, and the envoy from Amberpine Lodge had already become one of them before anyone thought to look.
sources: quest 12295 description and reward text (Ducal sent a week ago; hardy people who know the land)

parts.body: The same curse, which makes beasts out of people, has taken Solstice Village in the east, whose people gave themselves to the wolfcult.

title: Bloodmoon Isle
body: Bloodmoon Isle lies just off the eastern coast, a stronghold of the Bloodmoon worgen and the cultists who serve beside them. On it rises Shadowfang Tower, where a great worg keeps guard over a shade that bears the name of Arugal, the sorcerer of Dalaran who called the worgen into Silverpine and is said to have died years ago.

parts.body: On Bloodmoon Isle the shade of Arugal was beaten. It was not enough to finish him, but he will not be seen in these parts any longer.

title: Granite Springs
body: Granite Springs is a camp of bounty hunters in the shadow of Drak'Tharon Keep who pay well for ice trolls taken alive, hired by Conquest Hold and Amberpine Lodge alike. One of them wears a mask and can mingle with the trolls since his stay in the Ghostlands, and in a cage sits a Drakkari prisoner named Drakuru, who offers a truce sealed in blood: he knows things that will aid in the struggle here.

parts.body: Drakuru speaks of legendary artifacts, lost for thousands of years, made to render Drak'Tharon Keep impervious, and means to use them to cleanse the keep of the Scourge.

title: Drakil'jin Ruins
body: The Drakil'jin Ruins are haunted Drakkari ruins on the eastern coast, raised around a crypt. Drakkari oracles and protectors guard the grounds, great gongs stand outside, and within, long-dead warmongers walk again among guardian serpents. A mystic camped nearby hears the spirits of the Drakkari who came before crying out for a peace they cannot find.

parts.body: A corrupted warlord bars their rest. The Drakkari have become a lost people, fierce and savage, while their dead suffer through no fault of their own.

title: The Remains of Vordrassil
body: Long ago powerful druids planted a tree in the heart of the Grizzly Hills, meant to become a world tree. It was called Vordrassil, and once it was grown the druids decided, for reasons long forgotten, that it had to be destroyed. Its trunk splintered where it struck the ground, oozes crawl there, and in the hollow of its old trunk stands Grizzlemaw, the furbolg city, whose tribes, peaceful for thousands of years, are now at war.

parts.body: The furbolgs grew a sapling of Vordrassil to bring back their bear god Ursoc, who died in the War of the Ancients. He returned, filled with bloodlust like his people.
sources: quest 12207 description (druids planted it; to be a world tree; the earth's cries where the remains fell; ooze)

parts.body: Ursoc's freed spirit told why the old druids cut the tree down: Vordrassil's roots reach into the dwelling of an old god, Yogg-Saron, the beast with a thousand maws.

title: Westfall Brigade Encampment
body: The Westfall Brigade Encampment stands in the north of the hills, southwest of Thor Modan. Its soldiers have come a long way from Westfall in search of a road north, and here they have their hands full, with the Horde to the west and the iron dwarves to the east; most of their horsemen were left at the fight for Venture Bay.

parts.body: The tunnels beneath Thor Modan that might have carried the brigade toward Icecrown are blocked and unstable, some unused for generations.

title: Thor Modan
body: Thor Modan is the ancient capital of the iron dwarves, laid open since stone giants tore the land asunder thousands of years ago and collapsed part of the city. The sons of iron want it back, and they are besieged: stone giants hurl boulders into the trench, earthen battle their golems in the plaza, and their forgemaster urges his constructs on for the thane and for Loken. Torn pages of a journal litter the battlefield.

parts.body: The journal is Brann Bronzebeard's, and with a keystone the rune plates he followed gave up their words: 'The cradle of stone and iron.' 'Ulduar nestled in the storm.'
